 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. A key cog at outside linebacker on arguably the greatest New England football team of all time, the 2004 Patriots, Mike Vrabel absorbed a first-hand lesson on playing the Dolphins in Miami on Monday Night Football.
 The Patriots were rolling at 12-1hunting, the No. 1 seed in the AFC, while the Dolphins, at 2-11, were playing out the string in yet another lost season.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Who is A.J. Feeley?
 New England held a 28-17 lead in the fourth quarter at Pro Player Stadium, and then something happened.
 Miami happened.
 Somehow, behind the legendary A.J. Feeley – 8-10 as a starter in his NFL career – Miami rallied for the 29-28 win.
 This Patriots team is not as good as the 2004 team, and Miami isn't that bad.
 Sunday's battle is not the proverbial "trap game," for the Patriots. It's a "sink-hole game," one that could derail the season, and Vrabel knows it.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Bob DeChiara-Imagn Images
 Dolphins have heat advantage
 "I think that they've continued to improve, and I know that they're probably – and they should be – excited to play at home in front of their crowd," said Vrabel of the Dolphins, who picked up their first win on Sunday against the Jets. "We'll have to go on the road inside the division here and continue to improve."
 Vrabel was subdued in his Wednesday press conference, all business, like he understands his team is in for a fight.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The forecast for Sunday calls for temps in the 80s and typical Florida humidity.
 All hands on deck
 The Patriots have to be ready to play 60 minutes in that heat. Depth will be at a premium.
 "We have to be conditioned. I think the better that we play, the more we possess the ball, the fresher we'll stay defensively," said Vrabel. "Hopefully we get the receivers into a rotation. The backs, we rotate. I don't think that the offensive linemen will necessarily rotate. We may play a couple guys based on who's available. That remains to be seen. The edge guys, we rotate. We try to rotate along the defensive line. We like to have our best players available to help us win."
